newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease 0.36 pct in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease 0.36 pct in profit-taking.

text.p: Istanbul shares slipped lower in mild profit-taking on Friday, following a 9.3 percent surge in the last two days, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed at 86,983.93, down 315.36 points, or 0.36 percent from Thursday's all-time high 87,299.29. It brushed an early high of 88,255 before sales began.
Over the week, the index leapt 5.38 percent after last week's 1.5 percent drop.
Daily trade volume fell sharply to 22.65 trillion lira from Thursday's record high 31 trillion.
"The trade range was squeezed after the recent sharp gains. It was natural for profit-taking to follow, particularly in shares which had strong premiums," said Ibrahim Basnur from Ar securities.

Of the 229 shares traded, 115 declined, 69 advanced and 45 ended steady. The 85-share industrial index .ISEI lost 0.85 percent to 92,191.25 while the 15-share financial index .ISEF firmed 0.75 percent to 83,602.27.
Actives were led by largely state owned flat steel producer Eregli which spearheaded yesterday's rally. It dropped 750 lira to end at 13,750.
Other actives were T.Isbank's C series shares, up 250 lira at 16,250, largely state-owned petroleum refiner Tupras, steady at 26,500 lira and Turkish Airlines, up 750 lira at 26,000.
Turnover in the most heavily traded four stocks made up 34 percent of the total volume.
